long_biography.plain_text:
Finding a retired Baltic trader in Amsterdam gave Mark Hammond and Alison Brown the vessel for an unusually ambitious charter business. They bought her in 1986, restored traditional rigging with Dutch craftsmen and sailed her into the First Fleet re-enactment before returning to New Zealand. As Tradewind's captain, Hammond combined heritage sailing with remote expedition work, carrying small passenger groups to the Auckland Islands and taking the schooner on long ocean passages.

Otago Harbour remained the base for Hammond's commercial vessels for more than three decades. Through Discovery Maritime he operated the research vessel Geomarine from 1995, then the locally built expedition vessel Maia. The work placed practical seamanship at the centre of his career: restoring older ships, running charter expeditions and maintaining vessels for research in southern waters.
